item.title: On the dynamics of weighted shifts on Fr\'echet sequence spaces over trees
item.description: arXiv:2611.10053v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we give characterizations of Li--Yorke chaos, mean Li--Yorke chaos and distributional chaos for weighted backward shifts acting on general Fr\'echet sequence spaces over directed trees. As corollaries, we obtain explicit characterizations in the setting of K\"othe spaces $\lambda_p(A,V)$, where $p\in\{0\}\cup[1,\infty)$ and $V$ is a directed tree. In particular, we obtain criteria for the case of the classical Banach spaces $\ell^p(V)$, $p\in[1,\infty)$, and $c_0(V)$.
item.dc:creator: Mateus Azevedo, Fernando Costa Jr., Jo\~ao V. A. Pinto

item.title: Characterizations of minimal Hermitian completions via moments and subdifferentials
item.description: arXiv:2611.10323v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given a Hermitian matrix $A_0$ and a real subspace $W$ of Hermitian matrices, we study the matrices $A_0+W_0$, $W_0\in W$, of minimal spectral norm, which we call $W$-minimal. The main motivation is the Hermitian matrix completion problem, where $W$ is spanned by the Hermitian matrix units corresponding to the unspecified entries. Our main tool is the moment of a subspace $S\subseteq\mathbb{C}^n$ relative to $W$, a compact convex subset of $\mathbb{R}^r$, $r=\dim(W)$, which we relate to the joint numerical range and to the $k$-dimensional field of a family of matrices. We compute the subdifferential of $\|A_0+W(x)\|$ in terms of the moments of the eigenspaces of the extreme eigenvalues of $A_0+W(x)$, and we obtain several equivalent characterizations of $W$-minimality: in terms of eigenvectors, of moments, of subdifferentials and of norm one functionals that annihilate $W$. When the identity belongs to $W$, every $W$-minimal matrix has balanced spectrum, and minimality is equivalent to the moments of the eigenspaces of the maximum and minimum eigenvalues having nonempty intersection; we show that this characterization fails if $I\notin W$. We illustrate the results with several examples, and we prove that the adjacency matrix of a connected graph is minimal for its completion problem if and only if the graph is complete bipartite.
item.dc:creator: Tamara Bottazzi, Alejandro Varela

item.title: Basis selection, universal sampling discretization, and sampling recovery
item.description: arXiv:2611.10402v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every real $N$-dimensional subspace of $L_2$, we construct one orthonormal basis such that, for every $1\le v\le N$, at most $Cv\log(eN/v)$ positively weighted samples discretize the squared $L_2$ norm of all $v$-term combinations. Random rotations also give simultaneous weighted $L_p$ estimates and a sharp $C\log(eN)$ bound for the squared $L_2$ norm of the pointwise maximum. For prescribed coefficient classes, a change of measure yields sampling recovery estimates from $Cv\log^3(2v)$ samples under a lower Riesz inequality and a common square-integrable pointwise bound.
item.dc:creator: Feng Dai, Jiashu Ran, Vladimir N. Temlyakov

item.title: Analytic criteria for criticality of subordinated Schr\"{o}dinger operators
item.description: arXiv:2611.10614v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a subordinated Schr\"{o}dinger operator, we introduce a quantity that plays a role analogous to the bottom of the spectrum of a Schr\"{o}dinger operator, and establish analytic criteria for subcriticality, criticality and supercriticality of a subordinated Schr\"{o}dinger operator.
item.dc:creator: Takumu Ooi

item.title: Sharp Constants and First-Order Asymptotics in a Bourgain--Brezis--Mironescu Formula for Riesz Potentials
item.description: arXiv:2611.10656v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate sharp constants and asymptotic properties of a pointwise inequality of Bourgain--Brezis--Mironescu type in dimension \(n\geq2\), involving Riesz potentials and Spector's nonlinear fractional differential operator \(\mathcal D^\alpha\) of order \(0<\alpha<1\). For every \(n\geq3\) and \(0<\alpha<1\), we determine the optimal constant without symmetry restrictions and prove that it is attained by smooth radially monotone functions centered at the evaluation point. The proof combines geodesic-flow invariance, kernel monotonicity, and circular rearrangement. In dimension two, we establish the leading-order asymptotic behavior of the optimal constant and derive an explicit formula in the radial class. We further refine the pointwise limit established by A. Claros and C. P\'erez [Bourgain--Brezis--Mironescu formula for Riesz potentials, Adv. Math. 503 (2026), Art. 111226] by obtaining an explicit first-order correction with a quadratic remainder uniform in the spatial variable. Finally, we strengthen their convergence-in-measure result on compact subsets for functions in \(W^{1,1}(\mathbb R^n)\) by establishing almost-everywhere convergence as \(\alpha\to1^-\), without passing to a subsequence.
item.dc:creator: Mohamed Jleli, Bessem Samet

item.title: On S\l oci\'nski-type decomposition, BCL model and unitary extension of commuting Banach space Wold isometries
item.description: arXiv:2611.11536v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The adjoint of an operator plays the central role in Hilbert space operator theory. In particular, dilations of Hilbert space contractions, extension of commuting Hilbert space isometries to Hilbert space unitaries, orthogonal decompositions of contractions and functional models for commuting isometries are heavily dependent on the presence of adjoint. In this paper, we develop a theory of Banach space Wold isometries with right-complemented ranges by showing explicit constructions of Berger-Coburn-Lebow model and unitary extension for such isometric tuple without the help of adjoint. We also show that a S\l oci\'nski type decomposition is possible for such a commuting tuple of Banach space isometries. Each of our results generalizes the corresponding result in the Hilbert space theory.
item.dc:creator: Swapan Jana, Sourav Pal, Saikat Roy

item.title: Eccentricity in mutual strong Birkhoff-James orthographs of C*-algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.11703v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the eccentricity of every vertex in the orthograph of mutual strong Birkhoff-James orthogonality for arbitrary finite-dimensional C*-algebras and for the algebra K(H) of compact operators on an infinite-dimensional separable Hilbert space. This gives a more detailed description of the orthograph introduced by Aramba\v{s}i\'c et al. (Banach J. Math. Anal. 14 (2020), 1751-1772). As an application, we characterize scalar multiples of unitary elements among invertible elements of finite-dimensional C*-algebras in terms of eccentricity alone. We also show that M_3(C) is the only finite-dimensional C*-algebra whose orthograph has a non-trivial connected component of radius 3.
item.dc:creator: Srdjan Stefanovi\'c

item.title: Fredholm weighted composition operators on the Lipschitz space of a tree
item.description: arXiv:2611.11737v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathcal{L}$ be the Lipschitz space of a tree. In this paper, we establish a complete characterization of the weighted composition operator $W_{\psi,\varphi}$ to be Fredholm on $\mathcal{L}$. Applying our characterization, we describe the connection between the Fredholmness of $W_{\psi,\varphi}$ and that of the composition operator $C_\varphi$.
item.dc:creator: Junkai Kong, Lei Liu

item.title: Forelli--Rudin Type Operators in Infinite Dimensions, I
item.description: arXiv:2611.11984v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce Forelli-Rudin type operators on the open unit ball of $\ell^2$. The weighted $L^p$-$L^q$ boundedness of these operators are completely characterized for all $p,q\in[1,\infty]\times [1,\infty]$, and every Schatten class between the weighted $L^2$ spaces are also completely characterized. Meanwhile, we derive trace formulas for corresponding operators, which cannot be obtained from their finite-dimensional counterparts by formally replacing the dimension parameter with infinity. These results are not only infinite-dimensional extensions of those obtained by Cheng, Fang, Wang, and the second author (2017), Zhao and Zhou (2022), and Ding (2022). They also reveal new phenomena that are unique to infinite dimensions and arise from the geometric and measure theoretic differences between finite- and infinite-dimensional spaces. The key ingredient of our proofs is that we also establish the Forelli-Rudin type estimates in infinite dimensions, which may shew some night on the function theory in the infinite-dimensional unit ball.
item.dc:creator: Yu Hou, Jiayang Yu

item.title: Whitney-Type Real-Analytic Approximation on Banach Spaces I: The $C^0$ and $C^1$ Cases
item.description: arXiv:2611.12181v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The classical Whitney theorem on real-analytic approximation is a fundamental result in finite-dimensional analysis and geometry. Extending this theory to general infinite-dimensional Banach spaces involves longstanding open problems. This paper is the first part of our study of Whitney-type real-analytic approximation on Banach spaces, focusing on the $C^0$ and $C^1$ cases. We prove that a real Banach space admits a separating polynomial if and only if it admits a polynomial topological embedding into a real Hilbert space. We also introduce classes of mappings that locally factor through polynomial maps into finite-dimensional spaces and develop methods of real-analytic approximation for these classes. Using these tools, we establish fine $C^0$ and $C^1$ real-analytic approximation theorems for broad classes of Banach spaces, including nonseparable ones. As applications, we resolve several open problems, including those concerning Whitney-type extensions with real analyticity off closed sets, real-analytic approximation preserving Lipschitz constants, and the real-analytic equivalence of diffeomorphic open subsets of Hilbert spaces.
item.dc:creator: Zhouzhe Wang

item.title: On operators with many spectral components
item.description: arXiv:2611.12208v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a complex Banach algebra $\mathscr A$ with unit and $n\in\mathbb N$, let $\mathcal C_n(\mathscr A)$ be the set of all elements whose spectrum has at least $n$ connected components, and let $d_\sigma(\mathscr A)=\sup\{n;\;\mathcal C_n(\mathscr A)\neq\varnothing\}$ be the spectral depth of $\mathscr A$. We characterize nonemptiness of $\mathcal C_n(\mathscr A)$ in terms of orthogonal idempotents, compute $d_\sigma(\mathscr A)$ for finite-dimensional algebras, and show that every class $\mathcal C_n(\mathscr A)$ is open. For operators on an infinite-dimensional complex Banach space $X$ these classes are dense in $\mathscr B(X)$, which implies that $\mathcal C_\infty(\mathscr B(X))$ is a dense $G_\delta$-subset of $\mathscr B(X)$. By contrast, we exhibit a commutative Banach algebra whose spectral classes are all nonempty and none of which is dense. For self-adjoint operators on a Hilbert space, we obtain sharper perturbation results, with positive semi-definite perturbations of prescribed rank producing spectra with exactly $n$ components. We show that a quasinilpotent weighted forward shift $S_w$ on $X$ admits a nilpotent rank-one operator $F$ such that the spectrum of $S_w+\alpha F$ has infinitely many components for every nonzero $\alpha$.
item.dc:creator: Janko Bra\v{c}i\v{c}, Marko Kandi\'c

item.title: Completions of vector metric spaces and the diagonal property of order convergence
item.description: arXiv:2611.12365v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A vector metric space carries a distance with values in an ordered vector space $E$; a sequence converges if its distances to the limit are dominated by a sequence decreasing to zero in $E$. We show that, for Archimedean $E$, every $E$-valued vector metric space has a completion if and only if order Cauchy sequences in $E$ converge and $E$ has the diagonal property of order convergence (SDP): for every double sequence $(a^k_n)$ with $a^k_n\downarrow_n0$ there are indices $n_k$ and $e_k\downarrow 0$ with $a^k_{n_k}\le e_k$. In vector lattices this is the classical diagonal property of Kantorovich, equivalently the strong Egoroff property. We show that its standard characterisations remain valid in Archimedean ordered vector spaces, and that it holds if and only if convergence in every $E$-valued vector metric space satisfies the iterated limit axiom. For an ordered Banach space with a closed normal cone, all completions exist if and only if the norm is $\sigma$-order continuous; if the cone has an interior point, all vector metrics are then scalar. By a theorem of Veksler and of Hager and van Mill, for compact Hausdorff $K$ either $K$ is an almost $P$-space and $C(K)$-valued vector metrics are scalar, or there are countable $C(K)$-valued vector metric spaces without completion. A product of ordered vector spaces with (SDP) and nonzero cones has (SDP) if and only if there are fewer than $\mathfrak b$ factors, extending a result of Hager and van Mill for $\mathbb{R}^A$. We also prove permanence results for direct summands and uniformly dense vector lattice covers of pre-Riesz spaces.
item.dc:creator: C\"uneyt \c{C}evik

item.title: Vector metrics with values in pre-Riesz spaces I: transfer of order convergence along vector lattice covers
item.description: arXiv:2611.12376v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vector metric spaces in the sense of \c{C}evik and Altun take values in a vector lattice, but their axioms use only the order of the value space. We develop the theory for vector metrics with values in an Archimedean pre-Riesz space $E$, i.e.\ an ordered vector space admitting a bipositive order dense embedding $i$ into a vector lattice $Y$. We ask when an $E$-valued vector metric $d$ and the vector-lattice-valued metric $i\circ d$ have the same convergent and Cauchy nets and sequences. Relatively uniform convergence transfers along every cover. For nets, $\mathrm{o}_3$-convergence transfers if and only if the cover has an intrinsic domination property. This property holds for pervasive covers, by a result of Kalauch and van Gaans, for uniformly dense covers and in finite dimensions; it fails for an example of Kalauch and van Gaans. Sequential convergence transfers under a countable domination property implied by uniform density, but not under pervasiveness. For uncountable $\Gamma$, the vector lattice $\mathbb{R}\mathbf 1\oplus c_{00}(\Gamma)$ is pervasive in its Dedekind completion $\ell^\infty(\Gamma)$ without the transfer, while for countable $\Gamma$ the transfer holds; the difference is explained by order separability. In finite dimensions, with a closed generating cone, all these convergences coincide with norm convergence in every cover. For $C^1[0,1]$-valued integral metrics, positivity of the kernel on the diagonal forces all order convergences to coincide with $L^1$-convergence. For the Volterra kernel $(t-s)_+$, by contrast, $L^1$-convergence, relatively uniform convergence and order convergence are pairwise different, and we describe each explicitly.
item.dc:creator: C\"uneyt \c{C}evik

item.title: The symmetric Gaussian isoperimetric problem in the plane
item.description: arXiv:2611.12456v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We resolve the symmetric Gaussian isoperimetric conjecture in the plane: every minimizer of Gaussian perimeter among centrally symmetric sets of prescribed Gaussian measure is a centered ball, a symmetric strip, or the complement of one of these sets. A quadrant-reflection argument reduces the problem to unconditional sets. The planar structural results of Barchiesi, Cagnetti and Julin then leave only a noncircular strictly convex stationary oval. We exclude this oval by an explicit volume-preserving and perimeter-decreasing linear deformation, which geometrically corresponds to an "unconditional squeezing". More generally, without requiring any symmetry assumptions, we show that any noncircular closed embedded $\lambda$-self-shrinker is always unstable via linear deformations. We also record a reduction to the unconditional case in dimension three, using an orthogonal equipartition theorem of Musin.
item.dc:creator: Emanuel Milman

item.title: Gelfand and sampling numbers of weighted Wiener spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.12558v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The aim of this paper is to establish sharp asymptotic bounds on the Gelfand numbers of weighted Wiener spaces $\mathcal{A}^r_\theta$ measured in $L_q$. This is done by using results for Gelfand numbers of sequence spaces and applying them to each layer of a hyperbolic cross to obtain results for Gelfand numbers between different (weighted) Wiener spaces. These can then be used to establish bounds in $L_q$ by combining them with known results and techniques for Besov spaces. This significantly narrows a gap in the current research, since the Gelfand numbers provide a lower bound on the (non-linear) sampling numbers, whereas upper bounds on this quantity have been studied in multiple papers via an upper bound given by the best m-term approximation.
item.dc:creator: Moritz Moeller

item.title: Twisted convolution with conic support and the parabolic algebra
item.description: arXiv:2611.12631v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that tempered distributions on \(\mathbb R^{2n}\) whose supports satisfy a common strict cone condition form a unital associative algebra without zero divisors under twisted convolution \(\star\). The supports may be noncompact, and the associated Weyl maps need not be bounded. As applications, we show that the parabolic algebra and the norm-closed algebra generated by positive translations and modulations have no zero divisors, confirming Levene's conjecture. We also obtain a zero-product theorem for Toeplitz operators on the one-dimensional Fock space with bounded symbols whose distributional Fourier transforms satisfy a common strict cone condition. The proof of the distribution theorem uses Schwartz smoothing between distributional Weyl maps to convert a hypothetical zero product of nonzero distributions into a smooth function \(h\not\equiv0\) satisfying the same cone condition and \(h\star h=0\). The cone bound implies the \(Q\)-support condition, meaning that some linear functional is bounded above on \(\operatorname{supp}h\) and has compact upper level sets there. Truncating \(h\) near the maximum of this functional and applying the support identity for compactly supported twisted squares rule out \(h\star h=0\). For the operator applications, uniformly bounded Weyl-conjugation averages identify twisted convolution with bounded operator composition under the common cone condition.
item.dc:creator: Jie Qin

item.title: The vector-valued Stein inequality and dimension-free R-sectoriality
item.description: arXiv:2611.12645v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a complex Banach space \(X\), we characterise dimension-free \(R\)-sectoriality of the Walsh operator, the Ornstein--Uhlenbeck operator, the Laplacian, and the Poisson operator by the vector-valued Stein inequality. For each family, the dimension-free \(R\)-bound of the resolvents on the negative real axis equals the Stein constant. Consequently, the resolvent estimate on the negative real axis already implies uniform \(R\)-sectoriality at an angle strictly smaller than \(\pi/2\). We furthermore prove that the full and dyadic Stein properties are equivalent and that they are independent of the exponent \(1<p<\infty\) entering their definition.
item.dc:creator: Jan van Neerven

item.title: On Solvability of Irregular Infinite-Dimensional Differential-Algebraic Equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.12721v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates the solvability of infinite-dimensional differential-algebraic equations (DAEs) on Hilbert spaces. We focus on irregular systems for which the operator pencil is not surjective onto the full state space, but only onto a subspace determined by the algebraic constraints. We establish a Lumer-Phillips-type generation result for this class of systems, showing that dissipativity together with a partial surjectivity condition yields a contraction semigroup on the dynamic subspace. The resulting wellposedness conditions are compared with existing solvability results. We further extend the analysis to systems in which hidden algebraic constraints restrict the dynamics to a proper closed subspace of the dynamical subspace. Under an additional structural condition, we show that the resulting constrained system is $E$-radial on suitably chosen spaces. We also demonstrate that semigroup generation does not, in general, imply $E$-radiality on the original state spaces. This provides a Weierstra\ss-type decomposition useful for controller design. The framework is illustrated by some examples.
item.dc:creator: Ala' Alalabi, Lorena Bociu, Birgit Jacob, Kirsten Morris

item.title: Separable $\mathcal L_{\infty}$-spaces with Kalton's property $Q$
item.description: arXiv:2611.12764v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct separable $\mathcal L_\infty$-spaces with Kalton's property $Q$, which, to the best of our knowledge, are the first known examples of this kind. Our technique employs the Bourgain--Pisier construction and a quantitative analysis of metric types in limits of finite-dimensional $\eta$-admissible embeddings. The argument rests on two complementary estimates: approximate radial centres yield asymptotic separation of tree increments, while an admissibility inequality yields asymptotic gain, leading to concentration on Kalton's interlacing graphs. This leads to an abstract criterion for property $Q$ in terms of asymptotic separation $AS_\theta$ and asymptotic gain $AG_\alpha$. We illustrate the limitations of this criterion with Johnson--Lindenstrauss spaces. Our examples exclude uniform embeddings of the unit ball of $c_0$, strengthening in a nonlinear direction the classical Bourgain--Delbaen phenomenon. As an application, every separable Banach space embeds isometrically into a separable $\mathcal L_\infty$-space whose unit ball is not a uniform retract of the unit ball of its bidual.
item.dc:creator: Jes\'us Su\'arez

item.title: Concave shifts and the complete Nevanlinna--Pick property
item.description: arXiv:2611.12778v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathcal H$ be a reproducing kernel Hilbert space of holomorphic functions on the unit disc, and assume $\mathcal H$ is invariant under the forward and backward shifts. We show that if the forward shift on $\mathcal H$ is concave, then $\mathcal H$ is a complete Nevanlinna--Pick space. This gives an affirmative answer to the concavity part of Shimorin's question \cite{Sh02} and extends his theorem on the complete Nevanlinna--Pick property of Dirichlet-type spaces with superharmonic weights.
item.dc:creator: Shuaibing Luo, Eskil Rydhe

item.title: Extensions from Positive and Full Unit Spheres of $C^\infty([0,1])$ with a Compatible Fr\'echet Metric
item.description: arXiv:2611.12794v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study isometric extensions from positive and full unit spheres of $C^\infty([0,1],\mathbb F)$, where $\mathbb F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. We equip these spaces with a translation-invariant metric that induces the usual Fr\'echet topology, is unbounded, has convex balls, and has strictly increasing distances from zero along nonzero rays. Every surjective isometry of the pointwise positive unit sphere extends uniquely to a complex-linear surjective isometry of the complex-valued space. Restriction gives the unique real-linear isometric extension on the real-valued space. On the full unit sphere, every surjective isometry extends uniquely to a real-linear surjective isometry. The positive-sphere maps are compositions with the identity or an admissible reflection. The full-sphere maps also allow constant unimodular factors and, over the complex field, conjugation. We also classify the surjective ambient isometries. A counterexample shows that these metric properties alone do not guarantee positive-sphere extension. Under an explicit anchor condition, we classify surjective isometries of finite-order jet-positive spheres for maximum-type anchored metrics and prove that they extend uniquely to complex-linear surjective isometries. The classification allows any permutation of the anchored coordinates, combined with the identity or reflection on the highest-derivative component. The condition holds for every anchor when $m=1$ or $m=2$.
item.dc:creator: Min-Ruei Lin

item.title: A metric characterization of free unitary quantum groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.10299v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For a compact matrix quantum group $G$ with a fundamental unitary representation $u$ of dimension at least two, the reduced operator norm of the self-adjoint main character satisfies $\left \|\chi_u+\chi_u^*\right \|_{C_r(G)}\geq2\sqrt2$. Within the category of free quantum groups of Kac type, it is known that the minimum $2\sqrt2$ is attained only by free unitary quantum groups. We establish this characterization in full generality, including the non-Kac setting: this minimum is attained if and only if $G$ is isomorphic to a free unitary quantum group $U_Q^+$ as compact matrix quantum groups.
item.dc:creator: Yoonje Jeong, Sang-Gyun Youn

item.title: Weighted Logarithm Laws in non-commutative Probability
item.description: arXiv:2611.10387v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove analogues of weighted laws of iterated logarithm and laws of logarithm for non-commutative martingales and independent random variables respectively. First we obtain a weighted LIL for non-commutative martingales, extending the sharp unweighted result of arXiv:2509.22037v2 to the case for polynomial weights, then by approximation to a broader class of functions. Then we proved a weighted law of logarithm for triangular array of weights and replacing the coefficient in the denominator by regularly varying functions with index $\alpha$. We show that the normalised sums converge to 0 for $\alpha> 1/2$ and for the case $\alpha=1/2$, we obtain the sharp upper bound with constant $\sqrt{2}$.
item.dc:creator: Sourav Panja, Diptesh Saha

item.title: On the lower bound for the $L^1$ norm of Liouville exponential sums. II
item.description: arXiv:2611.10790v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\lambda$ denote the Liouville function, and put \[ I_\lambda(X)=\int_0^1\left|\sum_{n\le X}\lambda(n)e^{2\pi i n\alpha}\right|\,d\alpha. \] In this paper, we prove that \[ \limsup_{X \to \infty} \frac{\log I_{\lambda}(X)}{\log X} \ge \frac{1}{3}. \]
item.dc:creator: Ben Krause, Jiangpeng Li, Yu-Chen Sun, Hui Wang

item.title: Schauder exponential basis which is not Riesz
item.description: arXiv:2611.10799v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that there exists a Schauder basis $\{e^{i \lambda_n t}\}_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ with real frequencies in $L^2(-\pi,\pi)$ which is not a Riesz basis.
item.dc:creator: Andrei V. Semenov

item.title: Controlled Riemannian rigidity
item.description: arXiv:2611.10854v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Given a compact Lie group acting smoothly and freely on a compact connected manifold, we prove that the space of invariant Riemannian metrics whose symmetry group is precisely the group in question is open dense in that of all invariant metrics provided the orbit space is sufficiently large. This strengthens the author's prior results and recovers Ebin's to the effect that trivial-symmetry Riemannian metrics constitute an open dense set. In the process, the discussion also addresses a number of apparent gaps in said sources, pertaining to the rigidity results in question.
item.dc:creator: Alexandru Chirvasitu

item.title: Eaton Triples, Polar Representations, and Lie Triple Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.10859v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: An Eaton triple consists of a finite dimensional real inner product space, a closed subgroup of its orthogonal group, and a closed convex cone that meets every orbit and satisfies an extremal inner product inequality. In the literature on group majorization and invariant norms it is a standing hypothesis that the triple admits a reduced triple, obtained by restriction to the span of the cone. We prove that this is always the case: the axioms force the span of the cone to be a section of a polar representation, and Gichev's orbit intersection theorem applies. The reduced group is a finite reflection group, crystallographic when the group is connected; Eaton cones are its closed chambers, unique up to the group action; and a compact linear group admits an Eaton cone if and only if its representation is polar with a finite reflection group as Weyl group. For connected groups we construct a Lie triple system on the space, determined by the inner product and the orbits alone, for which the cone is a Weyl chamber; unlike Dadok's orbit equivalence with a symmetric space, it involves no choices.
item.dc:creator: Gabriel Larotonda, Tin-Yau Tam

item.title: On the Bendixson criterion for attractors of dynamical systems in metric spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.10918v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We revisit the Bendixson criterion for attractors, originally proposed by R.A. Smith for the finite-dimensional case and subsequently extended by M.Y. Li and J.S. Muldowney to Banach spaces. First, we give a concise proof of the criterion for general dynamical systems (semiflows, mappings, cocycles) in metric spaces using \v{C}ech cohomology. This approach allows for a significant weakening of previously known conditions while simultaneously resolving existing misunderstandings. Second, for compact invariant sets of semiflows that are topologically one-dimensional and possess zero first cohomology (e.g., attracting a superset with zero first cohomology), we prove that any chain recurrent point within the invariant set must be an equilibrium. In the proof, we construct a global strict Lyapunov function using Whitney-Bebutov sections. Third, we generalize and refine R.A. Smith's theorem concerning the finiteness of the set of fixed points for analytic mappings, as well as M.L. Cartwright's theorems on to almost periodic flows.
item.dc:creator: Mikhail Anikushin

item.title: Harmonic and Monogenic Representations of White Noise and its weighted harmonic Bergman estimates
item.description: arXiv:2611.11244v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Continuing Feichtinger's generalized stochastic process theory, we analyze harmonic and monogenic representations of white noise in Euclidean spaces. We define its convolution with square-integrable functions. Using the weighted Sobolev regularity of the white noise, we establish a high-dimensional Sokhotski-Plemelj formula for the white noise density. Furthermore, we embed these representations into new weighted Bergman spaces, proving that the weighted Bergman norms of the harmonic representations are bounded by the white noise's weighted Sobolev norms.
item.dc:creator: Fang Yang, Jiecheng Chen, Tao Qian

item.title: Rayleigh's conjecture in dimensions four and five
item.description: arXiv:2611.11250v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove Rayleigh's conjecture for the clamped plate in dimensions four and five. In fact, we obtain a sharp comparison with the first Dirichlet eigenvalue: on every open set of finite positive measure, the first plate eigenvalue is at least the square of the Dirichlet eigenvalue multiplied by the ratio attained on a ball. The proof uses a homogeneous transformation of a trial function and its gradient. Two divergence identities reduce the comparison to positivity of a quadratic form in the Hessian. We establish the required Bessel inequalities by rational estimates for entire profiles and their remainders. An exact defect identity accounts for regular nodal sets, so the argument allows trial functions of either sign and imposes no boundary regularity. The domains may be disconnected or unbounded. We characterize equality up to sets of zero Sobolev capacity. We also obtain quantitative stability with the optimal quadratic power of the Fraenkel asymmetry.
item.dc:creator: Durvudkhan Suragan

item.title: The Canonical Family of Reduced Row Pivot Echelon Forms and the Induced Lexicographic Canonical Algorithm for Linear Programming
item.description: arXiv:2611.11608v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A complete canonical family of uniquely normalized, row-equivalent representatives of an $m\times n$ matrix is introduced and termed the family of Reduced Row Pivot Echelon Forms (RRPEFs). All RRPEFs represent the same row space, with the standard reduced row echelon form, renamed the Upper RREF (URREF), and the Lower RREF (LRREF) as its extreme members. A reformulation of Noether's Complementary Subspace Basis Theorem yields normalized bases of the row space that coincide with the nonzero rows of the corresponding RRPEFs. Constructively, each RRPEF is obtained by multi-index Gauss--Jordan reduction of a nonsingular transition submatrix. Factoring the admissible pivot-index sets by equality of their associated RRPEFs yields a quotient set in canonical bijection with the set of distinct RRPEFs. This bijection transfers the strict lexicographic order to the distinct RRPEFs and induces a finite chain from the URREF to the LRREF. The resulting structure gives rise to the Induced Lexicographic Canonical Algorithm (ILCA). Lexicographic confinement and singular-transition skipping restrict the candidate domain, whereas RRPEF reuse and scalar-equivalent transition bypassing avoid redundant Gauss--Jordan reductions while retaining the corresponding basic-solution tableaux. Strict lexicographic progression prevents cycling, while the traversal proceeds independently of objective improvement under degeneracy-induced stalling. ILCA terminates when a feasible tableau satisfies the standard optimality conditions and otherwise completes the finite traversal, including for Tucker- and Cunningham-type totally degenerate configurations.
item.dc:creator: A. G. Paraskevopoulos, D. A. Patsouras

item.title: Adjoint Kernel Sensitivity of the Rough Heston Characteristic Exponent
item.description: arXiv:2611.11652v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multi-factor approximations of rough volatility kernels affect the characteristic exponents used in Fourier-based derivative valuation. We derive an adjoint representation for the first-order sensitivity of the rough Heston characteristic exponent with respect to its memory kernel, with model parameters and the input variance curve held fixed. The Volterra--Riccati functional $\mathcal L_T(K,z)$ admits a local real-analytic extension, jointly in the kernel perturbation and the transform parameter. The Fr\'echet derivative of this extension with respect to the kernel in $L^1$ is represented by integration against a continuous sensitivity kernel $B_K(u,z)$, obtained from a backward linear Volterra equation and independent of the perturbation direction. This representation resolves the leading-order contributions of kernel perturbations across memory lags. On the structural kernel class, which contains the fractional kernel and its multi-factor approximations and has empty interior in $L^1$, the extension yields Hadamard directional differentiability and a first-order expansion with a quadratic $L^1$-remainder for all sufficiently close structural kernels, uniformly on compact subsets of the strip of transform parameters. The same sensitivity kernel yields multi-factor weight and decay-rate derivatives. Numerical experiments at multi-factor reference kernels assess the finite-resolution implementation and illustrate how the lag distribution of positive perturbations with equal $L^1$ mass affects the first-order response.
item.dc:creator: Carlos Escudero, Francisco J. Luguera-Par\'uas, Miguel Sama

item.title: Extreme amenability and failure of the L\'evy property for the trace-class special unitary group
item.description: arXiv:2611.11944v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that the trace-class special unitary group, equipped with the trace-norm topology, is extremely amenable but is not a L\'evy group, answering questions posed by Pestov. The failure of the L\'evy property follows from a uniform non-concentration estimate for every nontrivial compact subgroup. Extreme amenability is established through a transverse spectral-gap estimate and trace-norm duality, yielding asymptotic invariance of Lipschitz observables under each fixed finite-dimensional special unitary subgroup. A limiting argument then gives fixed points for continuous actions on arbitrary compact Hausdorff spaces. We also formulate an abstract criterion for extreme amenability based on asymptotic quadratic invariance along a dense chain of compact subgroups. Neither argument uses concentration results for other Schatten exponents.
item.dc:creator: Sergio Luigi Cacciatori, Takashi Shioya, Pietro Ursino, Shigeaki Yokota

item.title: Controllability with and without Dissipation - a Port-Hamiltonian Approach
item.description: arXiv:2611.12145v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A port-Hamiltonian system with energy dissipation can be modelled by connecting a larger, non-dissipative system with a so-called closure relation. We study whether approximative controllability of the dissipative system is characterised by the same property of the larger system. The answer is negative in general, but positive for sufficiently well-structured systems - this is our main result. As a simple illustration, we show how approximate controllability of a wave equation implies approximate controllability of a heat equation.
item.dc:creator: Jochen Gl\"uck, Anthony Hastir, Birgit Jacob, Hannes Wagener

item.title: An almost sharp tomas-stein restriction theorem for a class of anisotropic operators
item.description: arXiv:2611.12463v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $d\geq 2$. For each $j\in \{1,\dots,d\}$, let ${\ell}_{j}\geq 1$ and $m_{j}\geq 2$ be integers, and let $a_{j}$ be a nonzero real number. We prove that the oscillatory integral operator \begin{equation*} T_{{\ell}_{1},\dots,{\ell}_{d},m_{1},\dots,m_{d}}f(x):=\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}} e^{\dot{\imath} \left(a_{1}x^{{\ell}_{1}}_{1}y^{m_{1}}_{1}+\dots +a_{d}x^{{\ell}_{d}}_{d}y^{m_{d}}_{d} \right)}f(y)dy,\;\;\; x\in \mathbb{R}^{d}, \end{equation*} satisfies the restriction estimate \begin{equation*} \|T_{{\ell}_{1},\dots,{\ell}_{d},m_{1},\dots,m_{d}}f\|_{L^{2}(\mathbb{S}^{d-1})}\lesssim \|f\|_{L^{p}(\mathbb{R}^{d})}, \end{equation*} for each $1\leq p\leq 2$, whenever $(\frac{\ell_{j}}{m_{j}}-\frac{1}{m_{j}}+1)\frac{2}{p^{\prime}}\geq 1$, for every $j\in \Gamma$, and \begin{equation*} \mathcal{E}:=\min{\left\{\min_{1\leq j\leq d}{\frac{m_{j}}{{\ell}_{j}}},\,\min_{1\leq k\leq d}{\frac{d-1}{\sum_{j\neq k} \frac{\ell_{j}}{m_{j}}+\frac{2}{m_{k}}}}\right\}}> \frac{2}{p^{\prime}}. \end{equation*} We also give counterexamples that show that the condition $\mathcal{E}\geq 2/p^{\prime}$ is necessary for this restriction inequality.
item.dc:creator: Ahmed A. Abdelhakim

item.title: Fixed-occurrence cases of the shuffle-word-embedding conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.12498v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For self-adjoint contractions in a finite tracial von Neumann algebra, binary shuffle traces with $m=1,2,4$ occurrences of the second variable admit simultaneous finite-dimensional approximation by commuting diagonal contractions. For every odd $m$, a commuting diagonal self-adjoint pair reproduces any prescribed finite set of shuffle traces exactly. When the first operator has finite spectrum and $m\geq3$ is odd, a weighted symmetric cycle reproduces all degrees simultaneously. We prove fourth-order trace-derivative positivity in finite tracial von Neumann algebras and obtain a positive measure representing the four-occurrence coefficients. For each even $m$, we characterize the contraction model property by positivity of an associated trace-derivative functional.
item.dc:creator: Trung Hoa Dinh

item.title: Singularising quantum channels preserving kappa-additivity
item.description: arXiv:2611.12537v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct quantum channels by averaging unitary shift conjugations with respect to $\kappa$-additive probability measures on measurable abelian groups. The channels act on the duals of operator algebras generated by shifts and bounded measurable multiplication operators. They preserve $\kappa$-additivity of quantum states and admit a weak-$*$ integral representation on this class. If the averaging measure vanishes on singletons, every output state is singular. In the appendix, we also establish the corresponding Fubini's theorem for $\kappa$-additive measures.
item.dc:creator: Sviatoslav V. Dzhenzher

item.title: The Douglas property for multiplier algebras of operators
item.description: arXiv:1107.0980v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a collection of reproducing kernels k which includes those for the Hardy space of the polydisk and ball and for the Bergman space, k is a complete Pick kernel if and only if the multiplier algebra of the Hilbert space H^2(k) associated to k has the Douglas property. Consequences for solving the operator equation AX=Y are examined.
item.dc:creator: Scott McCullough, Tavan T. Trent

item.title: Differentiation, Taylor series, and all order spectral shift functions, for relatively bounded perturbations
item.description: arXiv:2404.18422v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given $H$ self-adjoint, $V$ symmetric and relatively $H$-bounded, and $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{C}$ satisfying mild conditions, we show that the Gateaux derivative $$\frac{d^n}{dt^n}f(H+tV)|_{t=0}$$ exists in the operator norm topology, for every natural $n$, give a new explicit formula for this derivative in terms of multiple operator integrals, and establish useful perturbation formulas for multiple operator integrals under relatively bounded perturbations. Moreover, if the $H$-bound of $V$ is less than 1, we obtain sufficient conditions on $f$ which ensure that the Taylor expansion $$f(H+V)=\sum_{n=0}^\infty\frac{1}{n!}\frac{d^n}{dt^n} f(H+tV)\big|_{t=0}$$ exists and converges absolutely in operator norm. Finally, assuming that $V(H-i)^{-p}\in\mathcal{S}^{s/p}$ for $p=1,\ldots,s$ for some $s\in\mathbb{N}$ (for instance, when $H$ is an order 1 differential operator on an $s-1$ dimensional space), we show that the Krein--Koplienko spectral shift functions $\eta_{k,H,V}$, satisfying $${Tr}\left(f(H+V)-\sum_{m=0}^{k-1}\frac{1}{m!}\frac{d^m}{dt^m} f(H+tV)\big|_{t=0}\right)=\int_{\mathbb{R}} f^{(k)}(x)\eta_{k,H,V}(x)dx,$$ exist for every $k=1,2,3,\ldots$, independently of $s$. The latter result (which is significantly stronger than \cite{vNS22}) is completely new also in the case that $V$ is bounded. The proof is based on \cite{PSS}, combined with a generalisation of the multiple operator integral compatible with \cite{HMvN}. We discuss applications of our results to quantum physics and noncommutative geometry.
item.dc:creator: Arup Chattopadhyay, Teun D. H. van Nuland, Chandan Pradhan

item.title: Spectral Limits of the Neumann-Poincar\'e Operator on Degenerating Tori
item.description: arXiv:2410.20033v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We determine the limit of the spectrum of the Neumann-Poincar\'e operator on circular tori as the torus degenerates. As the central hole closes, the spectrum converges to $[-1/2,0]$ together with a set of positive points, which we characterize as eigenvalues of explicit limiting operators. As the cross-section shrinks, the spectrum converges to $[0,1/2]$.
item.dc:creator: Doosung Choi

item.title: Finite dimensional approximations for Hilbert space operators and applications in Quantum Mechanics
item.description: arXiv:2509.03384v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this work, we develop a unified framework for quasidiagonal and F\o lner-type approximations of linear operators on Hilbert spaces. These approximations (originally formulated for bounded operators and operator algebras) involve sequences of non-zero finite rank orthogonal projections that asymptotically commute with the operator -- either in norm (quasidiagonal) or in mean (F\o lner). Such structures guarantee spectral approximation results in terms of their finite sections. We extend this theory to unbounded, densely defined closable operators, establishing a generalization of Halmos' classical result: every closable quasidiagonal operator is a compact perturbation of a closable block-diagonal operator on the same domain. Likewise, we introduce sparse F\o lner sequences and establish an interplay between quasidiagonal approximations and the existence of sparse F\o lner sequences. The theoretical developments are illustrated with explicit examples using different types of weighted shifts and applied to quantum mechanical models, including a detailed treatment of the Weyl algebra and its Schr\"odinger representation.
item.dc:creator: Eva A. Gallardo-Guti\'errez, Fernando Lled\'o, Laura S\'aenz

item.title: Nearly invariant subspaces in the real Hardy space
item.description: arXiv:2604.10240v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The objective of this article is to study nearly invariant subspaces of the backward shift operator on the real Hardy space. We also investigate nearly invariant subspaces with finite defect, and as a consequence, provide a characterization for almost invariant subspaces of the backward shift operator.
item.dc:creator: Arshad Khan, Sneh Lata, Dinesh Singh

item.title: Multipoint Characterization of Higher-Order Sobolev Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2606.00897v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In the paper, we prove a rather general characterization of higher-order Sobolev spaces. We show that the $k\mathrm{th}$-order regularity, where $k \in \mathbb{N}$, is captured via inequalities involving $2^k$-tuples of points. In fact, in full generality, the obtained results characterize higher-order Sobolev spaces based on Banach function spaces. Moreover, we show an analogous characterization of higher-order H\"{o}lder spaces. Finally, we propose a way to use the obtained results to define higher-order Sobolev and H\"{o}lder spaces on metric measure spaces.
item.dc:creator: Kacper Kurowski

item.title: Hausdorff operators and fractional Hausdorff operators in the Dunkl setting
item.description: arXiv:2606.16197v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the boundedness properties of the Dunkl-type Hausdorff operator on generalized Dunkl-type Morrey spaces and generalized Dunkl-type Campanato spaces. Furthermore, we introduce the fractional Dunkl-type Hausdorff operator and study its boundedness from $L^p(\mathbb{R}, d\mu_\alpha)$ to $L^q(\mathbb{R}, d\mu_\alpha)$. We also establish the boundedness of the fractional Dunkl-type Hausdorff operator on generalized Dunkl-type Morrey spaces under suitable conditions. As a consequence of our main results, we derive several applications. Finally, we evaluate the exact norm of the Dunkl-type Hausdorff operator on Dunkl-type Morrey spaces and Dunkl-type Campanato spaces.
item.dc:creator: Sumit Parashar, Saswata Adhikari

item.title: Generalized Sobolev-Orlicz spaces based on the Riesz fractional gradient as interpolation and potential spaces
item.description: arXiv:2606.17770v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this work we establish that the recently introduced fractional Sobolev spaces based on the Riesz fractional gradient of Musielak-Orlicz functions by one of the authors, coincide with the space of Bessel potentials of functions on such generalized Orlicz setting. Moreover, we identify them as complex interpolation spaces, and exploiting the well known properties for interpolation of operators we obtain several structural properties for those spaces.
item.dc:creator: Pedro Miguel Campos, Guillermo Garc\'ia-S\'aez

item.title: Schwartz-Class Gabor Windows and the Balian-Low Classification
item.description: arXiv:2609.06255v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A lattice Gabor frame consists of a window function and its time-frequency shifts along a lattice. We classify the lattices that admit Schwartz-class and, equivalently, Feichtinger frame windows. Except for symplectically irrational lattices of critical covolume 1, we determine the lattice-dependent achievable window smoothness and decay using the scale of modulation spaces. For symplectically rational lattices, including the rational lattices typically used in digital applications, the classification is governed by an integer lattice parameter introduced herein, the symplectic index gap. Our results extend the classical and amalgam Balian-Low theorems. The companion paper "Tilings, Packings, and Smooth and Compactly Supported Gabor Windows" develops the associated tiling-packing theorem and compact-support constructions.
item.dc:creator: Andrei Caragea, G\"otz Pfander

item.title: Compact Quasi-Metric Spaces Are Expand-Contract Plastic
item.description: arXiv:2610.14301v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: On a totally bounded metric space, every non-contractive self-map is an isometry. For quasi-metric spaces this fails. Here quasi-metrics are $T_1$: $d(x,y)=0$ implies $x=y$. Zavarzina gave a hereditarily precompact counterexample and asked whether rigidity holds at least for bijections. The author's toll spiral (arXiv:2610.13973) shows that it does not. We prove that compactness restores it: every compact quasi-metric space is expand-contract plastic, that is, each of its bijective non-contractive self-maps is an isometry. Countable compactness suffices, as does compactness of the conjugate topology. Bijectivity is needed, even on a compact, hereditarily precompact space. For arbitrary non-contractive self-maps, we prove rigidity when the space is hereditarily precompact and its conjugate topology is sequentially compact, in particular when it is also Yoneda complete; neither hypothesis can be dropped. Such maps are then surjective. In both theorems the $T_1$ axiom can be weakened to $R_0$, $d(x,y)=0$ implies $d(y,x)=0$, if hereditary precompactness is taken to mean that every sequence has a left K-Cauchy subsequence; surjectivity then holds up to points at distance 0 both ways. The weaker $T_0$ axiom is not enough: there is a $T_0$ space, compact in both topologies and satisfying all the other hypotheses of both theorems, with a bijective non-contractive non-isometry. Finally, for an asymmetric norm in finite dimension, the classical theorem makes the symmetric unit ball and sphere rigid for all non-contractive self-maps, and the forward ones if the norm is $T_1$. In infinite dimension, the symmetric ball and sphere need not be plastic, and for the forward ones we pose the quasi-metric form of the unit-ball question of Cascales, Kadets, Orihuela and Wingler. The two theorems and the counterexamples of Section 6 are machine-checked in Lean, except the steps listed at the end.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Duzer

item.title: Reduced Embry characterizations of quasinormal operators
item.description: arXiv:2610.17303v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that, for any two integers $2\le m<n$, a bounded operator $A$ on a complex Hilbert space satisfying \[ A^{*k}A^k=(A^*A)^k, \qquad k\in\{m,n\}, \] is quasinormal. More generally, we show that the inequalities \[ A^{*m}A^m\ge(A^*A)^m \quad \text{and} \quad A^{*n}A^n\le(A^*A)^n \] already imply quasinormality. Together with the known single-exponent counterexamples, this completely resolves the reduced Embry problem for bounded operators: the identities $A^{*k}A^k=(A^*A)^k$, $k\in S\subseteq\{1,2,\ldots\}$, characterize quasinormality if and only if $S$ contains at least two distinct integers greater than one. We also resolve the flatness problem for operators of class $\mathcal A$: equality between two consecutive normalized moments $(A^{*n}A^n)^{1/n}$ and $(A^{*(n+1)}A^{n+1})^{1/(n+1)}$, with $n\ge2$, implies quasinormality. Both results rely on an interpolation estimate obtained either from Hansen's inequality or from the transformer inequality for weighted operator geometric means. The solution to the reduced Embry problem additionally uses an extremal argument for optimal power bounds.
item.dc:creator: Pawe{\l} Pietrzycki

item.title: Stable topology and stable compactness
item.description: arXiv:2610.22185v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: To solve a large class of noncompact problems ubiquitous in random functional analysis and its applications, most of compactness-based fundamental theorems established for normed spaces or locally convex spaces are required to be extended for random normed modules and random locally convex modules in an appropriate way of weakening compactness. To achieve this goal, in this paper we first develop stable set theory by introducing some new set-theoretic tools, then propose a class of topological spaces with a stable structure, called stable topological spaces, and in particular propose and systematically develop the theory of stably compact spaces, which is a natural generalization of that of compact spaces. The resulting theory is of independent interest from the perspective of general topology since its investigation requires an analysis of stratification structures coordinated with partitions of unity in a complete Boolean algebra. Finally, we show the power of the theory of stable compactness by establishing random Banach-Alaoglu, random James and random Banach-Bourbaki-Kakutani-\v{S}mulian theorems.
item.dc:creator: Tiexin Guo, Xiaohuan Mu, Pasqualetto Enrico, Qiang Tu, Guang Yang

item.title: Algebraic properties of Truncated Toeplitz $+$ Truncated Hankel operators
item.description: arXiv:2610.35897v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study the algebraic properties of $\mathcal{S}_\theta$ --- the class of truncated Toeplitz plus truncated Hankel operators --- on the model space $\mathcal{K}_\theta$. We also give a complete characterization of the intersection class of truncated Toeplitz and truncated Hankel operators. As a by-product of our findings, we give a complete characterization for $S_\theta$, where $\theta$ is a finite Blaschke product and also obtained the commutant of $S_\theta + S_\theta^{*}$ in that case.
item.dc:creator: Kritika Babbar, Satyabrata Majee, Amit Maji

item.title: Higher-order derivatives and their applications to diffeomorphism groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.40062v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we apply higher-order tangent bundles and higher-order derivative maps to study countable subgroups of the diffeomorphism group ${\rm Diff}(M)$ of a closed smooth manifold $M$. Using this framework, we introduce the concept of higher-order $\mu$-discreteness for subgroups $\Gamma < {\rm Diff}(M)$, and show that both the strong Novikov conjecture and the coarse Baum--Connes conjecture hold for countable groups with higher-order $\mu$-discreteness. Finally, we give examples showing that higher-order $\mu$-discreteness encompasses a strictly larger class of subgroups of $\operatorname{Diff}(M)$ than its lower-order counterpart.
item.dc:creator: Jintao Deng, Geng Tian

item.title: Nonisomorphic separable Banach spaces at Lipschitz distance one
item.description: arXiv:2611.06493v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct nonisomorphic separable real Banach spaces whose multiplicative Lipschitz distance is one. Building on OpenAI's graph-space construction, we arrange two sequences of graph spaces into countably many blocks and form two spaces that differ by a single additional block. This block distinguishes their linear structures: one space contains a complemented copy of $\ell_1(c_0(\ell_2))$, whereas the other does not. By mapping the additional block to increasingly late positions and rearranging the remaining blocks, we obtain homeomorphisms whose Lipschitz constants and those of their inverses tend to one, while both spaces and their norms remain unchanged.
item.dc:creator: Ryotaro Tanaka

item.title: Recurrent and rigid multipliers on commutative Banach algebras. The Fourier algebra
item.description: arXiv:2611.09186v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study recurrence, rigidity and uniform rigidity of multipliers on semisimple commutative Banach algebras. For a power-bounded multiplier $T$ on a Tauberian, self-adjoint algebra $\mathfrak{A}$, we show that $T$ satisfies each of these properties if and only if the multiplication operator on $C_0(\Delta(\mathfrak{A}))$ induced by the Gelfand transform of $T$ does. One consequence of our analysis is that, if $\Delta(\mathfrak{A})$ is $\sigma$-compact, then recurrence implies rigidity for such multipliers. We examine in detail the multipliers of the Fourier algebra $A(G)$. In particular, we show that recurrence of a multiplier of $A(G)$ is equivalent to recurrence of the corresponding multiplier on $C_0(G)$ when the connected components of $G$ are open. For multipliers that are not power bounded, a flexible construction based on chains of compact subgroups of a locally compact abelian group $G$ produces multipliers of $A(G)$ that are rigid but not uniformly rigid, and multipliers that are recurrent but not rigid, such that in each case the corresponding multiplier on $C_0(G)$ is uniformly rigid. Via the Fourier-Stieltjes transform, these results describe the recurrence and rigidity properties of convolution operators on $L^1(G)$.
item.dc:creator: Mar\'ia J. Beltr\'an-Meneu, Jorge Galindo, Enrique Jord\'a

item.title: Sharp double logarithmic $L^\infty$ bounds for second-order Sobolev functions in dimension four
item.description: arXiv:1301.2353v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Although $W^{2,2}(\mathbb{R}^{4})$ does not embed into $L^\infty$, we prove that radial symmetry allows the $L^\infty$ norm to be controlled by the homogeneous Sobolev seminorm $\dot H^2$, at the cost of a logarithmic correction involving a stronger H\"older-type norm. Our main result is a sharp double-logarithmic inequality with optimal leading constant $1/(8\pi^2\alpha)$. We also establish a single-logarithmic estimate and prove the sharpness of its threshold. The optimal lower bound is derived by analysing a biharmonic obstacle problem with H\"older-type obstacle. A tailored penalization argument yields existence, uniqueness, and regularity of the minimizer, while an explicit transcendental equation for the free-boundary radius determines the sharp constant through its asymptotic behavior. These results provide fourth-order, four-dimensional analogues of the two-dimensional first-order inequalities of Ibrahim--Majdoub--Masmoudi (\textit{Proc.\ Amer.\ Math.\ Soc.}, 2007), with potential applications to fourth-order semilinear evolution equations with exponential nonlinearities.
item.dc:creator: Mohamed Majdoub, Tarek Saanouni

item.title: The Brown measure of a sum of two free nonselfadjoint random variables, one of which is R-diagonal
item.description: arXiv:2209.12379v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Suppose that $X_1$ and $X_2$ are two $*$-free, possibly unbounded, random variables with Brown measures $\mu_{X_1}$ and $\mu_{X_2}$ respectively. Using properties of classic free additive convolution, we develop a method for calculating $\mu_{X_1+X_2}$ when $X_2$ is $R$-diagonal. This method determines a density relative to Lebesgue measure on an open set whose closure equals the support of $\mu_{X_{1}+X_{2}}$. We prove that $\mu_{X_1+X_2}$ has no singular continuous part, that its density is strictly positive on this open set, and we determine the masses of its atoms. Explicit calculations are possible in several important cases. As an application, we combine our Fuglede--Kadison determinant formula with known subordination convergence results to calculate the limiting logarithmic potentials of free multiplicative random walks. We identify the limit with the Fuglede--Kadison determinant formula for free multiplicative Brownian motion previously proved by some PDE methods.
item.dc:creator: Hari Bercovici, Yu Kitagawa, Ping Zhong

item.title: A reverse entropy power inequality for i.i.d. log-concave random variables
item.description: arXiv:2510.09206v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that $h_\infty(X+Y)\leq h_\infty(Z+W)$, where $X, Y$ are independent log-concave random variables, and $Z, W$ are exponential random variables having the same respective $\infty$-R\'enyi entropies. Analogs for integer-valued monotone log-concave random variables are also obtained. Our main tools are decreasing rearrangement, majorization, and the change of measure.
item.dc:creator: Zhen Fu, Jiange Li

item.title: On fractal minimizers and potentials of occupation measures
item.description: arXiv:2512.14248v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We highlight two basic types of variational problems and prove the existence of fractal minimizers through the direct method in the calculus of variations. By design these minimizers are H\"older curves or H\"older parametrizations of surfaces whose images generally have a non-integer Hausdorff dimension. Their origin is deterministic, but their regularity properties are roughly similar to those of typical realizations of stochastic processes. As a key tool and our main technical result, we prove novel continuity and boundedness results for potentials of occupation measures of Gaussian random fields. These results complement well-known results for local times, but hold under much less restrictive assumptions. In an auxiliary section, we generalize earlier results on nonlinear compositions of fractional Sobolev functions with $BV$-functions to higher dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Michael Hinz, Jonas M. T\"olle, Lauri Viitasaari

item.title: Ces\`aro means of firmly nonexpansive iterates need not converge strongly
item.description: arXiv:2605.25491v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Firmly nonexpansive operators arise naturally as resolvents of monotone operators and as generalizations of projections and proximal mappings in convex optimization and fixed point theory. While their iterates are known to converge weakly to a fixed point, strong convergence is not guaranteed (Genel and Lindenstrauss, 1975). Strong convergence of Ces\`aro means of iterates is also known to fail for general nonlinear nonexpansive mappings (Krengel and Lin, 1987). In this paper, we show that this failure persists in the much smaller class of firmly nonexpansive mappings. Using suitable meshes, we construct a new explicit family of counterexamples in infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces with the origin as the unique fixed point. In the harmonic case, the Ces\`aro means of the iterates remain bounded away from the origin. Another variant yields Ces\`aro means that converge strongly to the origin. A third variant presents Ces\`aro means whose norms oscillate in the sense that their liminf is zero while their limsup is positive. Thus the strong convergence conclusion in von Neumann's linear mean ergodic theorem does not extend to Baillon's nonlinear mean ergodic theorem, even for firmly nonexpansive mappings.
item.dc:creator: Heinz H. Bauschke, Tran Thanh Tung

item.title: Two-mode stability for multi-marginal optimal transport maps
item.description: arXiv:2606.23037v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish a two-mode stability theory for Monge solutions of the multi-marginal optimal transport problem with barycentric quadratic cost. The associated tuple of maps splits into an external barycentric mode and internal relative modes. A quadratic lower bound for the Kantorovich defect controls the internal modes and yields a square-root estimate without invoking any two-marginal map-stability theorem. The external mode is the optimal transport map from the fixed source to the Wasserstein barycenter. Combining the resulting two-mode estimate with M\'erigot's sharp theorem gives a $\frac{1}{4}$-H\"older estimate for general perturbations, while barycenter-preserving perturbations satisfy a $\frac{1}{2}$-H\"older estimate. We prove that both exponents and the dependence on the weights are optimal. We also examine the scope of such decomposition beyond the barycentric cost: collective-coordinate perturbations and uniformly concave costs of the sum retain the two-mode estimate, whereas the analyses of graph interactions, hedonic costs, and translation-invariant costs identify the two possible obstructions -- loss of relative coercivity and lack of stability for the remaining external modes.
item.dc:creator: Bang-Xian Han, Zhuo-Nan Zhu

item.title: The Zaporozhets-Tarasov Conjecture on Mean Distances
item.description: arXiv:2608.06470v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For a convex body $K \subset \mathbb R^d$ let $\Delta(K)$ be the expected distance between two independent uniform points of $K$, and let $\theta(K)$ be the corresponding expectation for normalized surface measure on $\partial K$. The Zaporozhets-Tarasov conjecture asserts $\Delta(K) \le \theta(K)$. We prove this conjecture in case $d=2$. In addition, we give a six-vertex convex polytope in $\mathbb R^3$ for which the reverse strict inequality holds, and obtain counterexamples in every dimension $d \ge 3$ by taking products with segments.
item.dc:creator: Eric Shen

item.title: A Time-Frequency Framework for GKP Codes
item.description: arXiv:2609.10802v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a time--frequency framework for lattice GKP codes in which ideal codewords are realized in the modulation space $M^\infty$ and identified, through a vector-valued Zak transform, with a finite logical fibre over the continuous syndrome torus. Multi-window Gabor analysis then represents the logical vector by a finite block of adjoint-lattice coefficients. We prove that the normalized block map is an isometry, obtain an explicit recovering projection, and derive stable logical reconstruction. We further construct normalizable GKP approximants as lattice-envelope Gabor multipliers and establish weak-$*$ convergence and asymptotically isometric encoding. Finally, we recover displacement syndromes from phase relations between translated coefficient blocks and quantify their stability under additive perturbations.
item.dc:creator: Franz Luef, Eduard Ortega

item.title: A New Approach to Universal Measurability
item.description: arXiv:2609.14414v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: V. Fedorchuk, A. Chigogidze and T. Banakh in 2003 and V. Bogachev in 2024 posed the following questions: (i) is it true that $P_\tau(X)$ is $C$-embedded in $P_\sigma(X)$; (ii) is it true that $P_R(X)$ is $C$-embedded in $P_R(\beta X)$ if and only if $X$ is pseudocompact, where $P_\sigma$, $P_\tau$ and $P_R$ are the functors of probability measures on the space $X$ that are, respectively, $\sigma$-additive on the Baire $\sigma$-algebra, $\tau$-additive, and Radon? The answers to these questions are negative. In this paper the questions are put into a general framework: for spaces of measures $Q_p(X)\subset Q_q(X)$ of various types we study when $Q_p(X)$ is $C$-embedded ($C^*$-embedded) in $Q_q(X)$. It is proved that for spaces of alternating measures $M_p(X)\subset M_q(X)$ the $C$-embeddedness, the $C^*$-embeddedness and the $G_\delta$-density of $M_p(X)$ in $M_q(X)$ are equivalent, and a criterion in terms of sequences of continuous functions is given. The question of $C$-embedding of measure spaces is an extension of the question of coincidence of measure spaces, which is a development of the classical concepts of universally measurable and universal measure zero sets. Note (corrected version): incorrect statements of the previous versions are marked or removed; see the last section of the paper.

item.title: A Dimension-Free Bound on the Poincar\'e Constant of Isotropic Log-Concave Measures
item.description: arXiv:2610.07728v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Kannan--Lov\'asz--Simonovits (KLS) conjecture asserts that isotropic log-concave probability measures have Poincar\'e constants bounded by a universal constant, independently of dimension. In this work, we provide a deterministic variational proof that the Poincar\'e constant $C_P(\mu)\le25$, where $\mu$ is any isotropic log-concave probability measure. The proof centers on mean-zero integration of compatible symmetric tensor fields. Starting from constant tensors, we obtain factorially normalized Appell polynomials by iterating this procedure. Using moment estimates and a quadratic variance inequality, we establish geometric bounds on these iterated primitives through a \emph{joint} variational argument over the measure and test function. At a maximizing pair, stationarity in the test function controls the weighted sum of the two highest-order cumulant terms arising from the measure variation. To extend these bounds to arbitrary compatible fields, we use a weighted Helmholtz--Hodge decomposition of weighted divergence, the formal adjoint of differentiation. Controlling the curl in the decomposition yields a curvature comparison for the integration operators, uniformly in tensor order. Combining this comparison with the Appell bounds gives a bound on the full integration operator and hence the stated Poincar\'e inequality. The estimate is independent of the auxiliary positive curvature, allowing approximation to general isotropic log-concave measures.

item.title: $L_p$-spaces, $1\leq p\ne 2<\infty$, associated with type III and semifinite von Neumann algebras are not isomorphic
item.description: arXiv:2610.11055v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $M$ be a type III von Neumann algebra, and let $N$ be a semifinite von Neumann algebra. We prove that the Banach space $M_*$ does not embed isomorphically into the Banach space $N_*$. More generally, we prove that $L_p(M)$ is not isomorphic to a subspace of $L_p(N)$ for $1\le p<2$. In particular, the Banach isomorphism class of $L_p(M)$ distinguishes type III algebras from semifinite algebras for $1\le p<\infty$, $p\ne2$. This answers several long-standing open questions in the literature.
item.dc:creator: Jinghao Huang, Fedor Sukochev

item.title: Bijective Non-Contractive Maps of Hereditarily Precompact Quasi-Metric Spaces Need Not Be Isometries
item.description: arXiv:2610.13973v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Zavarzina asked whether every bijective non-contractive self-map of a precompact quasi-metric space is an isometry. We show that it need not be, even when the space is hereditarily precompact. On the integers, take the distance of an irrational rotation and add a fixed toll $c>0$ to every step from a nonnegative integer down to a smaller one. The resulting space, the toll spiral, is a hereditarily precompact quasi-metric space, and the shift $n\mapsto n+1$ is a bijective non-contractive map that is not an isometry. The construction works over any metric space $Y$: for every bijective isometry $\sigma$ of $Y$ and every point whose $\sigma$-orbit is aperiodic and totally bounded, adding the same toll along the orbit gives such a counterexample, for instance over the $p$-adic odometer. The conjugate of the toll spiral is not even precompact, so the hypothesis on the conjugate in Zavarzina's positive result cannot be dropped, even for bijections. The toll spiral is also not expand-contract plastic, since the inverse shift is a non-expansive bijection that is not an isometry. For an arbitrary bijective non-contractive map $F$, the distance from $F^kx$ to $F^ky$ has a limit as $k\to-\infty$; $F$ is an isometry for this limit, and the excess $D_0$ of the distance over it is the defect. On a hereditarily precompact space, we prove a monochromy theorem: if a pair $(a,b)$ has positive defect $\eta$, then there are natural numbers $t_1<t_2<\cdots$ such that either $D_0(a,F^{-\Delta}a)>\eta/4$ for every difference $\Delta=t_j-t_i$ with $i<j$, or $D_0(F^{-\Delta}b,b)>\eta/4$ for every such $\Delta$. Three boundary results delimit the remaining question; the open case, that of separated spaces compact in one of their topologies, has since been settled by the author (arXiv:2610.14301). The construction, in general and for the circle, is machine-checked in Lean 4 using Mathlib, with no unproved steps.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Duzer

item.title: Fitting Gaussian vectors in normed spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.20299v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Given a family of $N$ i.i.d. Gaussian points in a $d$-dimensional normed space, what is the probability that some linear transformation maps it to the unit sphere? The case of a Euclidean space is known as the ellipsoid fitting problem and has recently attracted major attention. We initiate a study of this fitting problem in a general normed space, both asymptotically and in a fixed dimension. We specifically focus on the space $\ell_\infty^d$, where a combinatorial reformulation allows us to show that $cd^2/\log d$ points can be fitted with high probability. We illustrate that the geometry of the normed space is reflected in the fitting problem by showing that in dimension $2$, the spaces $\ell_2^2$ and $\ell_\infty^2$ are characterized by having extremal fittability properties.
item.dc:creator: Guillaume Aubrun, Emmanouil Stavrakakis

item.title: A Pricing and Hedging Framework for Infinite-Dimensional Financial Markets
item.description: arXiv:2610.24169v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we provide a comprehensive study of how the classical Black--Scholes-type market framework behaves in an infinite-dimensional setting. The asset prices are modeled by stochastic evolution equations in a separable Hilbert space. The evolution of the risk-free asset and the corresponding discounting operators are governed by a strongly continuous group of bounded linear operators. Accordingly, we consider contingent claims with Hilbert-space-valued payoffs, whose values are discounted through the corresponding operators. Within this framework, we investigate the pricing and hedging of contingent claims, deriving the corresponding Hilbert-space-valued Black--Scholes equations and establishing exact replication results for both strong and mild solutions. We also study the special case where the infinitesimal generator is given by $A=rI$, allowing for real-valued contingent claims. We further investigate no-arbitrage and market completeness, introducing a Hilbert lattice structure to formulate arbitrage and characterizing attainability through operator equations associated with martingale representations. We also establish asymptotic completeness through finite-dimensional noise truncations. We introduce geometric Brownian motions in Hilbert spaces and derive sufficient conditions for the existence and uniqueness of an equivalent risk-neutral measure, together with explicit pricing formulas for some tractable examples. These results extend key aspects of the classical Black--Scholes framework to markets with infinite-dimensional asset-price dynamics. As a concrete application, the model can be interpreted as a segmented market consisting of a sequence of one-dimensional geometric Brownian motions.
